overview.description: Getaway is a Punjabi-origin shedding game in which players race to empty their hands while avoiding pickup penalties triggered by off-suit breaks (tochoo or thulla).

history.origins: Documented as a Punjabi family and social game under names including Getaway and Bhabhi, with related forms in Bangladesh and South India.
timeline: 20th century: Established as a regional shedding game in Punjab households.
2000s onward: Spread through online descriptions and diaspora play groups.
2020s: Rule descriptions and variant notes expanded to include regional forms such as Donkey.
history.evolution: Core mechanism remained stable: follow suit when possible, and interrupted tricks force card pickup by highest led-suit player.
history.cultural: Modern rulesets increasingly prefer neutral naming while preserving traditional gameplay.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack with rank order A K Q J 10 9 8 7 6 5 4 3 2.
setup.dealing: Deal all cards as evenly as possible clockwise; some players may have one extra card.

rules.objective: Get away by shedding all cards; last player still holding cards loses.
rules.gameplay: Opening trick: Ace of Spades holder leads, everyone contributes one card, and this first trick is always discarded. From second trick onward, leader is highest card of previously led suit. Players must follow led suit if they can. If a player cannot follow and plays another suit (tochoo), trick ends immediately and later players do not play to that trick. Highest card of the led suit picks up all cards played to that interrupted trick and leads next. If everyone follows suit, trick goes to waste and highest led-suit player leads next. Players who empty hand are out, except a player with lead power may need to draw from waste and continue under common rule.
keyRules: First trick is a mandatory full trick and always discarded.
From trick two onward, first valid off-suit break immediately stops trick.
Interrupted trick pickup goes to the highest card of led suit, not to the breaker.
Some tables allow taking all cards from immediate-left active player before a trick.

strategy.basic: Avoid becoming temporary high card on suits where later players are likely void.
strategy.intermediate: Manage lead control so that dangerous suits are led when opponents behind you are still likely to follow.
strategy.advanced: Use pickup and optional take-from-left timing to rebalance suit distribution and avoid forced endgame draws.
tips: Winning tricks is useful only when it helps you shed safely.
Track which players are likely void in each suit to predict interruption risk.

list.name: Take from Left
list.description: Before a trick, a player may take all cards from immediate-left active player in many local rules.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes only who may take cards and when; no engine constant overrides documented yet.

list.name: Counterclockwise Direction
list.description: Some tables play and deal in anticlockwise direction with mirrored take-card rule.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Direction and take-from-neighbour side are procedural; no engine overrides mapped for this variant.

list.name: Donkey
list.description: Related Kerala variant introduces trump suit when first off-suit is played.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Donkey adds trump and different trick resolution; full engine overrides would require separate Donkey spec.

difficulty.easy: Follows suit and sheds random cards without interruption planning.
difficulty.medium: Tracks likely void suits and avoids taking obvious pickup risks.
difficulty.hard: Optimizes lead and card height by seat order to minimize interrupted-trick liability while shedding quickly.

considerations: AI objective is conditional: winning a normal trick may be good, but winning interrupted-trick liability is bad.
Seat order matters because interruptions truncate trick participation.

play_card.description: Play a card to trick; follow suit when possible, otherwise play off-suit break when void.
play_card.constraints: Off-suit break from trick two onward stops trick immediately.

draw.reason: No stock draw phase is used in Getaway.

discard.description: Move normal completed trick cards to waste pile.
discard.constraints: Opening trick always discarded; later only non-interrupted tricks discarded.

pass.reason: Players respond with cards; off-suit break is a play, not a pass.

meld.reason: No meld declarations are used in Getaway.

go_out.description: Exit active play after shedding all cards, subject to lead-power exceptions.
go_out.constraints: Player may need to redraw from waste if they should lead but hand is empty.

trickConfig.leadRestrictions: Ace of Spades holder leads opening trick.

edgeCases.text: All players contribute to opening Ace of Spades trick and it is always discarded.
After first off-suit break, no further players contribute to that trick.
If empty-handed player must lead, they draw one random waste card and continue.

customLogicNeeded: Interrupt trick immediately when valid off-suit break occurs after first trick.
Implement pickup assignment to highest led-suit card holder.
Optional pre-trick action to take all cards from immediate-left active player.

customActions.description: Optional local-rule action to take all cards from immediate-left active opponent before a trick.

engine.deckDescription: The deck is a standard fifty-two-card pack without jokers; four suits of thirteen ranks each are used for trick play with no trump in the base game, and rank determines trick winner.
engine.suitDescription: The four French suits are Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades; there is no trump suit in the base game, so the highest card of the led suit wins the trick.
engine.rankDescription: Rank order from high to low is Ace, King, Queen, Jack, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2; players must follow suit if able, and the highest card of the suit led wins the trick.
engine.dealPattern: Deal full deck as evenly as possible clockwise.

hero.title: GETAWAY
hero.subtitle: Punjabi Shedding Game
hero.tagline: Shed fast and avoid the pickup trap.

synthesis.shortDescription: Avoidance shedding game where off-suit breaks can dump trick cards back onto the current high player.

prompts.human: Getaway: lead safely, read void suits, and avoid ending up as highest of led suit when interruption is likely.
prompts.ai: Game: Getaway. Opening trick always discarded; later off-suit break ends trick and forces highest led-suit player to pick up cards. Last player with cards loses.

scoring.description: No formal point count is required; hand loser is the final player still holding cards.
scoring.winCondition: Avoid being the last remaining player with cards.
